individual_results.question: Can I claim deductions under both Section 80C and Section 80D in the old tax regime? What are the maximum limits and who is eligible?
individual_results.answer:
Yes, you can claim deductions under both Section 80C and Section 80D in the Old Tax Regime. 

**Maximum Limits:**
- **Section 80C**: Up to ₹1,50,000 per financial year.
- **Section 80D**: There is no specific cap mentioned for Section 80D under the Old Tax Regime.

**Eligibility:**
Both deductions are available to individuals and HUFs.
individual_results.ground_truth: Yes, both can be claimed simultaneously under the Old Tax Regime. Section 80C: maximum deduction Rs.1,50,000 per year for individuals and HUFs. Eligible investments include PPF, ELSS, NSC, 5-year FD, life insurance premium, EPF, home loan principal repayment, and children tuition fees. Section 80D: maximum Rs.25,000 for health insurance premium for self/spouse/children (Rs.50,000 if the insured is a senior citizen). Additional Rs.25,000 for parents health insurance (Rs.50,000 if parents are senior citizens). Maximum total 80D = Rs.1,00,000 (self plus senior citizen parents). Both 80C and 80D are Chapter VI-A deductions and are completely blocked under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC). Neither can be claimed in the New Regime.

## Overview

Section 80C of the Income Tax Act allows individuals (and HUFs) to claim deductions of up to **₹1,50,000** per financial year from their gross total income. This is available **only under the Old Tax Regime**. Under the New Tax Regime, Section 80C deductions are **not applicable**.

---

## New Tax Regime vs Old Tax Regime — Rental Income

| Deduction | Old Regime | New Regime |
|---|---|---|
| Municipal Taxes | Allowed | Allowed |
| Section 24(a) — 30% standard deduction | Allowed | Allowed |
| Section 24(b) — Home loan interest (let-out) | Allowed (no cap) | Allowed (no cap) |
| Section 24(b) — Home loan interest (self-occupied) | Allowed (up to Rs.2L) | NOT allowed |
| Section 80C (ELSS, PPF, home loan principal) | Allowed | NOT allowed |
| Section 80D (Health Insurance) | Allowed | NOT allowed |
| Section 80EEA (First home buyer extra interest) | Allowed (if eligible) | NOT allowed |

**KEY RULE:** Sections 80C, 80D, 80EEA are Chapter VI-A deductions. They are completely
blocked under the New Tax Regime. Section 24(a) and 24(b) for let-out property are
income computation rules (not Chapter VI-A), so they apply under BOTH regimes.

---

## Overview

Section 80D allows deduction for **health insurance premiums** paid for self, family, and parents. Available under **Old Regime only**. Not available under New Tax Regime.

---

## Deduction Sections

### Section 80CCD(1) — Employee's Own Contribution

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Eligible amount | Up to 10% of Basic Salary |
| Overall cap | Within ₹1,50,000 (80C limit) |
| Regime | Old Regime only |

### Section 80CCD(1B) — Additional Employee Contribution

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Eligible amount | Up to ₹50,000 |
| Nature | **Over and above** the ₹1,50,000 80C limit |
| Total max benefit | ₹1,50,000 (80C) + ₹50,000 (80CCD1B) = **₹2,00,000** |
| Regime | Old Regime only |

### Section 80CCD(2) — Employer's Contribution

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Private sector | Up to 10% of Basic Salary |
| Government employees | Up to 14% of Basic Salary |
| Nature | Separate from 80C; deducted from gross salary |
| Regime | **Available in BOTH Old and New Regime** |

## Limit

- **Maximum deduction**: ₹1,50,000 per year
- If total of all 80C investments exceeds ₹1,50,000, only ₹1,50,000 is allowed as deduction
- Additional NPS investment beyond 80C → covered under **Section 80CCD(1B)**

New Tax Regime is better for this salaried employee.

individual_results.question: What deductions are available for interest paid on a home loan under Sections 24(b) and 80EEA? Can both be claimed together?
individual_results.answer:
Under the Old Regime, Section 24(b) allows a deduction of up to Rs.2 lakh per year for home loan interest on self-occupied property. For let-out property, the actual interest paid is deductible in full.

Section 80EEA provides an additional deduction of up to Rs.1.5 lakh per year for first-time home buyers who meet specific conditions, such as a home loan sanctioned between April 2019 and March 2022, and a stamp duty value not exceeding Rs.45 lakh.

Both deductions can be claimed together if the individual meets all eligibility criteria for both sections. However, Section 80EEA is only available under the Old Regime and is not applicable under the New Tax Regime.
individual_results.ground_truth: Section 24(b): For self-occupied property, maximum Rs.2,00,000 per year under Old Regime only. Not allowed under New Regime for self-occupied property. For let-out property, actual interest paid (no cap) is deductible under both regimes. Section 80EEA: Additional deduction of Rs.1,50,000 for first-time home buyers. Conditions: loan sanctioned between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022, stamp duty value of property must not exceed Rs.45 lakh, taxpayer must not own any other residential property on loan sanction date. Both 24(b) and 80EEA can be claimed together for self-occupied property under Old Regime, giving total interest deduction up to Rs.3,50,000 (Rs.2L plus Rs.1.5L). Section 80EEA is a Chapter VI-A deduction and is NOT available under New Tax Regime.

## Section 80EEA — First Home Buyer (Old Regime Only)

Eligibility conditions (ALL must be satisfied):
- Home loan sanctioned between 01-Apr-2019 and 31-Mar-2022
- Stamp duty value of property does not exceed Rs.45 lakh
- First time home buyer (no other residential property on date of sanction)
- Not already claiming Section 80EE deduction

Maximum deduction: Rs.1,50,000 per year (over and above Section 24(b))
**NOT available under New Tax Regime.**

## Common Misconceptions (Frequently Hallucinated)

1. **WRONG:** "Claim Section 80C under New Regime for rental income."
   **CORRECT:** 80C is blocked under New Regime regardless of income type.

2. **WRONG:** "Section 24(b) is capped at Rs.2 lakh for let-out property."
   **CORRECT:** The Rs.2 lakh cap applies ONLY to self-occupied property. For let-out, actual interest is deductible in full.

3. **WRONG:** "Section 24(a) is optional — you need bills to claim it."
   **CORRECT:** Section 24(a) is a mandatory 30% deduction from NAV. No bills required. It always applies.

4. **WRONG:** "You can deduct the full HP loss against salary income."
   **CORRECT:** HP loss set-off against other income is capped at Rs.2 lakh per year. Balance is carried forward.

5. **WRONG:** "Section 80EEA is a universal deduction for home loan interest."
   **CORRECT:** It has strict eligibility conditions (loan date, stamp duty limit, first-time buyer).

|---|---|---|
| Municipal Taxes | Allowed | Allowed |
| Section 24(a) — 30% standard deduction | Allowed | Allowed |
| Section 24(b) — Home loan interest (let-out) | Allowed (no cap) | Allowed (no cap) |
| Section 24(b) — Home loan interest (self-occupied) | Allowed (up to Rs.2L) | NOT allowed |
| Section 80C (ELSS, PPF, home loan principal) | Allowed | NOT allowed |
| Section 80D (Health Insurance) | Allowed | NOT allowed |
| Section 80EEA (First home buyer extra interest) | Allowed (if eligible) | NOT allowed |

**KEY RULE:** Sections 80C, 80D, 80EEA are Chapter VI-A deductions. They are completely
blocked under the New Tax Regime. Section 24(a) and 24(b) for let-out property are
income computation rules (not Chapter VI-A), so they apply under BOTH regimes.

individual_results.question: My employer deducted TDS, but I also earned interest from fixed deposits and savings accounts. Do I still need to file an Income Tax Return, and which ITR form should I use?
individual_results.answer: Yes, you still need to file an Income Tax Return. You should use **ITR-1** if your total income is less than Rs.50 lakh and there are no capital gains. Report the FD interest in the "Income from Other Sources" schedule, claim TDS credit from Form 26AS, and any applicable deductions like savings interest under Section 80TTA (Old Regime only, max Rs.10,000).
individual_results.ground_truth: Yes, filing is mandatory if total gross income exceeds the basic exemption limit. FD interest is taxable as Income from Other Sources. Bank deducts TDS at 10% under Section 194A if FD interest exceeds Rs.40,000 per year (Rs.50,000 for senior citizens). Even if TDS is deducted, you must file ITR to report all income and claim refund if excess TDS was deducted. Savings account interest: deductible up to Rs.10,000 under Section 80TTA in Old Regime only. ITR Form: Use ITR-1 (Sahaj) if total income is up to Rs.50 lakh and income sources are salary, one house property, and other sources (FD interest, savings interest). Use ITR-2 if income exceeds Rs.50 lakh or if you have capital gains or multiple house properties.
contexts:
## Who Must File an Income Tax Return?

Filing an ITR is mandatory if ANY of the following conditions apply:
1. Gross total income (before deductions) exceeds the basic exemption limit:
   - Old Regime: Rs.2,50,000
   - New Regime: Rs.3,00,000
   - Senior Citizens (60-79 years): Rs.3,00,000 (Old Regime)
   - Super Senior Citizens (80+ years): Rs.5,00,000 (Old Regime)
2. You have deposited more than Rs.1 crore in bank accounts in a year
3. You spent more than Rs.2 lakh on foreign travel in a year
4. You spent more than Rs.1 lakh on electricity in a year
5. You have foreign assets or foreign income
6. You are a company or firm (irrespective of profit or loss)
7. TDS or TCS has been deducted and you want to claim refund

Even if TDS is fully deducted by employer, you MUST still file ITR if:
- You have other income (FD interest, savings interest, rental income) that exceeds limits
- You want to claim a refund of excess TDS
- Your total gross income exceeds the basic exemption limit from all sources combined

---

## Common Scenario: Salaried + FD Interest

If you are a salaried employee with TDS deducted by employer AND you have FD interest income:
1. You MUST file ITR (FD interest is income from other sources)
2. Use ITR-1 if total income < Rs.50 lakh and no capital gains
3. Report FD interest in "Income from Other Sources" schedule
4. Claim TDS credit from Form 26AS
5. Claim savings interest deduction under Section 80TTA (Old Regime only, max Rs.10,000)
6. If excess TDS was deducted, you will receive a refund

---

## Which ITR Form to Use?

### ITR-1 (Sahaj) — Simplest Form
**Who can use:**
- Resident individual (not HUF or company)
- Total income up to Rs.50 lakh
- Income sources: salary/pension + one house property + other sources (FD interest, savings interest, family pension)
- Agricultural income up to Rs.5,000

**Who CANNOT use ITR-1:**
- If you have capital gains (stock, mutual fund, property sale)
- If you have more than one house property
- If you are a director in a company
- If you have foreign assets or foreign income
- If total income exceeds Rs.50 lakh

### ITR-2 — For More Complex Income
**Who should use:**
- Income above Rs.50 lakh
- Capital gains from sale of property, shares, or mutual funds
- More than one house property
- Foreign assets or foreign income
- Director of a company or has unlisted shares
- Non-resident or not ordinarily resident

### ITR-3 — Business/Profession Income
- For individuals/HUFs with income from business or profession
- Freelancers, consultants, professionals (doctors, lawyers, CAs)
- Partners in a firm

### ITR-4 (Sugam) — Presumptive Taxation
- For freelancers/small businesses opting for Section 44ADA or 44AD
- Total income up to Rs.50 lakh
- Cannot have capital gains or foreign income

---

## Step-by-Step ITR Filing Process

1. Download Form 26AS and AIS from IT portal
2. Compare with Form 16 — resolve any discrepancies
3. Check all interest income in AIS against bank statements
4. Go to IT portal -> e-File -> File Income Tax Return
5. Select Assessment Year (AY 2026-27 for FY 2025-26)
6. Use "Pre-fill" — portal auto-populates salary, TDS, and some income from Form 26AS and AIS
7. Verify pre-filled data carefully — do not blindly accept
8. Add any income NOT pre-filled (FD interest from small banks, savings interest, etc.)
9. Claim deductions (Old Regime: 80C, 80D, 80TTA etc)
10. Verify total tax calculated, compare with TDS deducted
11. Pay any remaining tax (self-assessment tax) before filing
12. Submit and e-verify using Aadhaar OTP, net banking, or DSC

---

## Form 16 — TDS Certificate from Employer

Form 16 is issued by the employer to every salaried employee by 15 June after the end of the financial year.
It is the primary document for filing ITR for salaried individuals.

### Part A — TDS Summary
- Employer name, address, TAN, PAN
- Employee name and PAN
- Quarter-wise summary of TDS deducted and deposited with government
- Acknowledgement number of TDS deposited

### Part B — Salary and Deduction Details
- Gross salary: basic pay, HRA, LTA, special allowance, perquisites
- Exemptions claimed: HRA exemption under Section 10(13A), LTA under Section 10(5)
- Standard deduction: Rs.50,000 (Old Regime) or Rs.75,000 (New Regime)
- Income chargeable under "Salaries"
- Deductions under Chapter VI-A: 80C, 80D, 80CCD(1B), 80TTA etc (Old Regime only)
- Net taxable income
- Tax payable / refundable
- TDS deducted from salary

Key action: Verify that your Form 16 Part A TDS figures match Form 26AS exactly.
Any mismatch can cause ITR processing delays or tax notices.

individual_results.question: What documents are required while filing an Income Tax Return for a salaried individual, and how should Form 16, AIS, and Form 26AS be used during the filing process?
individual_results.answer:
To file an ITR for a salaried individual for FY 2025-26, you need:

1. **Form 16**: Issued by your employer, it provides TDS details.
2. **AIS / TIS**: Contains all income and transaction data.
3. **Form 26AS**: Verifies tax credits.

**Usage During Filing:**

1. **Download Form 26AS and AIS from the IT portal** to get an overview of your tax liabilities.
2. **Compare with Form 16** to resolve any discrepancies in TDS amounts.
3. **Check all interest income in AIS** against bank statements for accuracy.
4. **Go to the IT portal -> e-File -> File Income Tax Return** and select AY 2026-27.
5. **Use "Pre-fill"**: The portal auto-populates salary, TDS, and some income from Form 26AS and AIS.
6. **Verify pre-filled data carefully** before accepting it blindly.
7. **Add any income NOT pre-filled**, such as FD interest.

Form 16 provides essential TDS details, while AIS and Form 26AS help in verifying the accuracy of your income and tax credits during the filing process.
individual_results.ground_truth: Form 16: TDS certificate from employer. Part A shows TDS deducted and deposited with PAN of employer. Part B shows salary breakup, allowances, perquisites, and deductions claimed. Form 26AS: Tax credit statement showing all TDS deducted against your PAN from all sources (employer, bank, buyer). Always verify Form 16 matches Form 26AS to avoid notices. Annual Information Statement (AIS): Comprehensive statement of all financial transactions linked to PAN including salary, FD interest, dividends, mutual fund transactions, property sales. Other documents: bank statements for interest income, home loan interest certificate for 24(b), investment proofs for 80C (PPF passbook, ELSS statement), health insurance receipt for 80D, rent receipts for HRA, Form 16A from bank for FD TDS. Process: Download Form 26AS and AIS from income tax portal. Pre-fill ITR using these. Reconcile with Form 16. Report all income including FD interest and dividends.

## Form 26AS — Tax Credit Statement

Form 26AS is maintained by the Income Tax Department and linked to your PAN.
It shows ALL tax deducted/collected at source from ALL deductors, not just your employer.

### What is in Form 26AS?
- Part A: TDS deducted on salary (by employer — Section 192)
- Part A1: TDS deducted on other income (by banks on FD interest — Section 194A)
- Part B: TCS (Tax Collected at Source) by sellers
- Part C: Advance tax and self-assessment tax paid directly
- Part D: Refunds received from Income Tax Dept
- Part F: TDS on rent, professional fees, etc.

### Why Form 26AS is Critical
- It is the official record of tax credit against your PAN
- Use it to verify TDS from employer, bank, and any other deductor
- If a bank deducted TDS on FD interest, it will appear in Part A1
- Any discrepancy between Form 16 and Form 26AS must be resolved before filing

How to download: Income Tax portal (incometax.gov.in) -> e-File -> Income Tax Returns -> View Form 26AS
